sections.label: TARGET — original human shot 0003

sections.label: ROUND 6 — MOTION via multiple KEYFRAMES (vendor @ImageN method)
sections.params: 8s · 720p · 16:9 · audio off · WINNER = K1 (3 ordered keyframes) · fal reference-to-video HONORS @Image keyframe directives
sections.shared_prompt_note: Correcting round 5's 'hold steady' mistake: the shot is motion through beats. Per the ByteDance vendor guide (sd25-pe, Keyframe Anchors), pass the real beat frames as ordered reference images (image_urls order = @Image1..N) and declare roles verbatim in the prompt. Face-free crops (hands+tape+lockset) keep it R3-safe. Result: real hand motion AND the tape stays short (the middle keyframe anchors it). This is the reproducible recipe for beat-based action. i2v first+last alone (K2) is NOT enough — the unconstrained midpoint over-extends.

experiments.approach: ★ 3 ordered KEYFRAMES (vendor @Image1/2/3) — reference-to-video
experiments.note: ★ THE MOTION FIX. Three real beat frames passed as image_urls=[kf1,kf2,kf3] with the vendor's verbatim directives ('Use @Image1 as the first frame', '@Image2 defines the second keyframe', 'Use @Image3 as the last frame', 'Use @Image1 through @Image3 as keyframes in that order'). fal's reference-to-video HONORS them: the clip opens on kf1, passes through kf2, ends on kf3 with genuine hand MOTION — and the tape stays correctly SHORT the whole time (the middle keyframe kf2 anchors it, killing the over-extension). R3-clean (face-free crops), no invented logo. Caveat: kf3 shows the tape being lowered, so it ends 'measure then lower' rather than a clean read-hold — pick/ýreorder a 'held across knob' last frame for a cleaner ending.
